facts.advisory_summary:
jackson-databind: InetSocketAddress deserialization triggers eager DNS resolution (SSRF) — ## Summary
`JDKFromStringDeserializer` constructed `InetSocketAddress` with `new InetSocketAddress(host, port)`, which performs eager DNS name resolution for hostname inputs at deserialization time. An application that binds untrusted JSON into a type containing an `InetSocketAddress` field issues an attacker-chosen DNS query during `readValue`, before any application-level validation or connect logic. The fix uses `InetSocketAddress.createUnresolved(host, port)`, deferring DNS to an explicit connect.

`Snappy.arrayCopy(Object src, int offset, int byteLength, Object dest, int destOffset)` called a native `memcpy` without validating the ranges. A negative or oversized `byteLength` or offset read or wrote outside the arrays and crashed the JVM. `SnappyOutputStream.rawWrite` and `SnappyInputStream.rawRead`, and therefore the typed-array `write`/`read` methods, pass caller-supplied ranges to this method.

### Patches
Fixed in 1.1.10.9 (#741). `Snappy.arrayCopy` checks both ranges before

expect.note: Snappy.arrayCopy is reached only via typed-array SnappyOutputStream.write/SnappyInputStream.read with caller-supplied ranges; ZooKeeper SnapStream (the only user, SnapStream.java:111/147) uses byte streams on local snapshots, with internal ranges, and only when snappy compression is enabled (off by default).
